config._comment: Listing Page Product Sequencing — v3. Built to the tiering + page order in 'FA Listing Sequence Algorithm'. Everything here is changeable without a deploy.

window._note: Flower orders are sliced to the 30 days ending 22 Sep 2026. The GA4 extracts for flowers, combos and hampers each arrived without a stated range and are assumed to match. Combo and hamper orders come from PDP Purchase, whose window is also unstated. Confirm before quoting figures.

denominators._note: The PRD defines both as '÷ clicks', which is what is set here. Switch either to 'pdp_views' in the viewer to see the effect: 15 hampers and 3 combos have zero PLP clicks, and among those that do, rates above 100% are common because orders and add-to-carts arrive from routes that never touched this listing.

config._floor_note: A product below this many impressions is not scored on its own rates; it takes the median score of its own bucket. Without it, smoothing hands a no-data product the page-average rate and it outranks products with real measured performance.
config._band_note: The PRD says 'Above ₹2500', which leaves a product priced exactly ₹2,500 in no bucket. Set to >= 2500 here to close it. Nothing is priced there today.
config._template_note: 30 positions, repeating every batch per the PRD. Counts: L 7, M 5, U 4, H 2, V 2, C 5, P 5 = 30.
config._precedence_note: A SKU is claimed by the first bucket it qualifies for and removed from the rest, so it appears once. Combo and Hamper outrank price bands.
config._fallback_note: The PRD says an empty pool borrows from a later batch, which cannot terminate once a pool is globally exhausted. Instead: a price slot falls through to the nearest band by price, then to the best remaining product of any bucket. C and P fall straight through to best remaining.

boost._comment: Up to 4 insertions per 30-slot set, sitting OUTSIDE the 30 — a set with x insertions displays 30+x. Base order is never changed. A SKU already placed is skipped, as is an out-of-stock one. Empty list means no insertions, per requirement 7.
boost._index_note: position 5 means the boost becomes the new #5 and the previous #5 shifts to #6.
